sections.context: The comprehensive product plan defines a clean Rust, Tauri, and Leptos platform spanning exact catalog history, KiCad libraries, project intelligence, PocketBase collaboration, inventory, procurement, and design reuse. Existing CSV and CAD data are import inputs rather than an executable Python or PyQt compatibility contract. A flat task dump or layer-by-layer rewrite would obscure user outcomes, create false dependencies, and prevent agents from completing independently testable vertical slices in the isolated Linux environment.
sections.approach: Organize delivery as ten outcome-oriented epics. Decompose each epic into tracer bullets that cross domain, persistence, application, UI, and integration seams far enough to prove a real workflow. Rust, Tauri, and Leptos are the only supported application implementation, PocketBase is the selected team backend, and Linux is the primary complete AFK integration lane. Mainline tools and KiCad 10 are pinned while scheduled compatibility lanes detect upgrades. Every frontend seed owns its automated journeys, semantic and accessibility assertions, deterministic screenshots, and agent visual self-review. Windows and macOS are later native release gates rather than blockers for every Linux tracer. Attach dependencies only between concrete child seeds where execution truly requires earlier evidence or an interface.

alternatives.name: Mirror every product-plan bullet as a seed
alternatives.rejected_because: It would create a noisy backlog of layer tasks without independently verifiable outcomes or useful ready-queue ordering.

alternatives.name: Chain roadmap phases as a strict waterfall
alternatives.rejected_because: Many domain experiments and adapters can proceed safely in parallel; blocking whole epics would hide valid work and slow feedback.

alternatives.name: Keep the prototype operational until parity
alternatives.rejected_because: Python and PyQt are not supported product scope. Immutable input fixtures and loss-detecting imports preserve valuable data without turning prototype behavior into a migration gate.

alternatives.name: Track work in Markdown checklists
alternatives.rejected_because: Seeds is the git-native source of truth for status, acceptance, dependencies, and readiness; parallel checklists would drift.

steps.title: Prove a Linux-first Rust product foundation
Give Engineers an exact revisioned KiCad catalog
Protect known-good baselines and close engineering defects
Adopt release switch and roll back libraries safely
Turn saved KiCad projects into actionable parts intelligence
Let small teams collaborate safely from desktop and web
Know usable inventory without false precision
Turn material demand into reviewed supplier handoffs
Reuse proven circuit blocks across organizations
Validate and release the Rust product across Linux, Windows, and macOS

risks: A clean implementation can silently lose uncommon source data; every import tracer uses immutable fixtures, field and byte manifests, and actionable parity reports.
Premature dependencies can make independent discovery and domain work disappear from the ready queue.
PocketBase or supplier assumptions can age quickly; versions are pinned, upgrades are rehearsed, and unresolved behavior remains a focused investigation seed rather than an untested fact.
Linux integration success can conceal native path, dialog, credential, installer, filesystem, or graphics failures; Windows and macOS remain explicit distribution gates.

Screenshot self-review can become ceremonial; seed acceptance requires a stable state matrix, semantic and accessibility assertions, retained diffs, recorded critique, and iteration on every material issue.
acceptance: Every confirmed product capability and roadmap exit condition is owned by exactly one outcome epic or an explicitly referenced cross-epic acceptance check.

Each epic is decomposed into independently verifiable vertical tracer seeds before implementation begins, and dependencies are attached at the narrowest concrete seed level so the ready queue exposes useful work.
Rust, Tauri, and Leptos are the only supported application implementation; existing catalog and CAD inputs remain read-only fixtures, and no Python or PyQt compatibility gate is required.

PocketBase is the only planned team-backend adapter and its protected commands, authorization, realtime recovery, migrations, upgrades, S3-compatible backup, and blank-environment restore receive real-process evidence.
Every frontend seed declares and runs its browser or native journey, semantic and accessibility assertions, materially distinct screenshots, and an agent visual self-review with required iteration.
The Linux AFK lane is isolated from host KiCad and user state, pins exact tool and KiCad versions, emits a complete evidence manifest, and has a separate scheduled newest-KiCad-10 compatibility lane.

Before Windows or macOS distribution, that native platform passes its release matrix for builds, paths, dialogs, credentials, installers, updater, filesystems, process launch, and host KiCad discovery.
No implementation seed authorizes unsafe mutation of an open KiCad project, editable library, immutable release, or operating-system-installed library.

sections.context: The product is a Rust, Tauri, and Leptos application for people who already use KiCad, so KiCad 10 is a required dependency rather than something automation must avoid. The existing CSV catalog and local CAD assets are migration inputs; Python and PyQt are not supported runtimes or parity targets. PocketBase is the selected team backend. Development and validation run natively on Windows for now; the Docker lab stays in the repository but is deferred to kicad-parts-c748. CI runners are expected to have KiCad installed.
sections.approach: Retain the completed loss-detecting Rust import fixtures as the migration oracle without executing or preserving the PyQt application. Keep the Rust workspace gate (cargo test, fmt, clippy -D warnings, and the import fixture check) green natively on Windows. Prove two vertical tracers. First, a real-catalog Tauri and Leptos journey whose symbol and footprint previews are SVGs rendered by the installed KiCad 10 kicad-cli and cached by library content and KiCad version. Second, a PocketBase collaboration and S3-compatible backup and restore journey against real disposable PocketBase and MinIO processes. Wherever KiCad already does the job, call it instead of reimplementing it. Keep a short manual checklist only for behaviour kicad-cli cannot show.

alternatives.name: Keep PyQt running as the migration oracle
alternatives.rejected_because: Python and PyQt are no longer supported scope; checked-in source data and expected artifacts provide a smaller and more durable import contract.

alternatives.name: Draw symbols and footprints with application-owned rendering
alternatives.rejected_because: It reimplements KiCad's drawing, drifts from what KiCad shows, and costs far more than calling the kicad-cli every user already has. With KiCad 10.0.4 a single part exports in about 0.25 s, and all 35 repository libraries in about 11 s (measured 2026-10-08).

alternatives.name: Keep KiCad out of automation and rely on manual Windows checks
alternatives.rejected_because: Every user has KiCad installed, and CI runners will too. Banning it forced redrawing and left interoperability untested.

alternatives.name: Make Docker the only development environment
alternatives.rejected_because: Windows-native development is simpler for now. The Docker lab is deferred to kicad-parts-c748, not deleted.

alternatives.name: Mock PocketBase and S3 in every integration test
alternatives.rejected_because: Unit tests may fake application-owned interfaces, but authentication, realtime behavior, migrations, backups, and blank-state recovery require the real disposable services.

steps.title: Boot an isolated Docker application-development stack
Exercise the real catalog and exact CAD previews through the Rust desktop
Prove PocketBase collaboration and S3-compatible recovery

risks: A fixture can accidentally encode Python implementation details; assertions must cover stable source fields, bytes, semantic content, diagnostics, and generated KiCad-compatible artifacts.

kicad-cli output, flags, or file naming can change between KiCad 10 releases. Record the KiCad version with each cached preview, key the cache by it, and cover export in automated tests against the installed version.
Each kicad-cli call costs about a quarter of a second. Batch whole-library exports and serve previews from the cache, so browsing never waits on the CLI.
A missing, moved, or unsupported KiCad installation can leave previews blank. Discovery must report the problem in the UI with a fix rather than failing silently.
Windows-only validation can hide Linux or macOS path, case, and line-ending behaviour. .gitattributes keeps fixtures byte-exact, and the release epic revisits the other platforms.

A database-only backup can appear successful while losing managed files; recovery tests verify relational records, PocketBase-managed files, separately stored objects where enabled, and hashes after restoring into blank isolated state.
acceptance: Rust tests inventory all 21 current categories and 178 rows, substitutes, local CAD references and assets, byte and semantic hashes, and the intentional distinction between 21 generated SQLite tables and 19 descriptor entries; a controlled fixture mutation produces an actionable field-level diff without invoking Python or PyQt.

The Rust workspace gate (cargo test, cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -D warnings, and the legacy import fixture check) passes natively on Windows from a fresh clone. The Docker lab and its full run are deferred to kicad-parts-c748.

The application finds the installed KiCad 10 kicad-cli, both in standard install locations and through a user override, and records its version. When kicad-cli is missing or unsupported, the UI shows how to fix it.

The Tauri and Leptos application searches at least 20,000 rows within the product target. It previews the exact selected symbol, including each unit, and footprint as SVGs produced by `kicad-cli sym export svg` and `kicad-cli fp export svg`. Previews come from a cache keyed by library content hash and KiCad version, so repeat views do not re-run the CLI. When an export fails, the UI shows the CLI's message.

Every frontend journey emits test results, accessibility evidence, and screenshots of all materially distinct states at stable viewports; the implementing agent records a visual and UX self-review and iterates until no material issue remains. Journeys run against a real KiCad 10 installation.

The real PocketBase service executes authentication, an optimistic protected command, second-client realtime notification, stale conflict, disconnect and checkpoint reconciliation, and a migration or upgrade rehearsal.

PocketBase backup artifacts are written to an isolated MinIO S3-compatible bucket; after deleting disposable PocketBase state, restore into a blank instance reproduces records, managed files, separately protected objects where enabled, and expected hashes.
No alternate-backend adapter, comparison harness, Python runtime, or PyQt compatibility gate is introduced. No application code redraws symbols or footprints that kicad-cli can already export.

name: Windows-first Rust application foundation tracer bullets

sections.context: The checked-in CSV catalog and local CAD libraries are source inputs for the new Rust product, not an active Python or PyQt workflow that must remain compatible. The target platform needs stable part and asset identities, immutable revision history, optimistic conflict handling, exact provenance and licensing, and a deterministic KiCad projection. The safest path is to prove the model on one representative real category before attempting a complete import. Development and validation run natively on Windows with disposable PocketBase and MinIO processes (mx-4c3a0d, tooling/native-services) and the installed KiCad 10. Where this plan says Linux journeys, read them as the hidden-desktop Windows journeys in apps/desktop/journeys.
sections.approach: Start with the existing resistor category and its local CAD references. Import it idempotently into canonical Catalog records with stable IDs, full initial snapshots, asset/blob/revision separation, and an explicit Change Set, while producing a zero-loss report against the source-fixture oracle. Then exercise one real Engineer edit through the Tauri and Leptos UI, protected command boundary, audit, conflict, restore, PocketBase realtime plus checkpoint reconciliation, and staged KiCad projection. Prove schema-bearing taxonomy and reviewed supplier-category mapping on the same slice. Only after those contracts pass, import the complete catalog and demonstrate deterministic projection. Source CSVs and local libraries remain byte-for-byte unchanged throughout the pilot.

alternatives.name: Design and migrate the full schema in one pass
alternatives.rejected_because: It would combine identity, revisions, assets, taxonomy, backend, UI, and projection risks before any real end-to-end path proves their contracts.

alternatives.name: Keep CSV rows as the canonical mutable model
alternatives.rejected_because: CSV cannot safely express optimistic commands, immutable history, exact asset bindings, team authorization, or auditable restores.

alternatives.name: Use event deltas as the only historical representation
alternatives.rejected_because: Immutable full revision snapshots make exact reconstruction, diff, restore, migration, and KiCad projection simpler and more robust for this domain.

steps.title: Import one complete legacy category into canonical revisions
Publish conflict and restore one Managed Part with exact CAD revisions
Classify one part through versioned taxonomy and reviewed supplier mapping
Prove lossless full-catalog migration and deterministic KiCad projection

risks: A normalization pass can silently discard blank strings, uncommon columns, category-specific fields, substitutes, or intentionally unprojected categories; every import produces a field-level loss report.
Logical assets, stored bytes, and semantic revisions can be conflated; raw blob hashes, revision snapshot hashes, provenance, and license declarations have distinct authority and tests.
Operational supplier, inventory, scan, or draft facts can accidentally create catalog revisions; revision commands accept only semantic catalog changes.
A projection failure can corrupt active KiCad state; generation always stages, validates, and atomically activates an isolated test-owned target with rollback evidence.
A visually plausible catalog can still be unusable or inaccessible; every new Tauri or Leptos state requires semantic, keyboard, accessibility, and inspected screenshot evidence.
acceptance: The current resistor category imports idempotently with stable part IDs, immutable IPNs, initial full Part Revisions, exact local CAD asset bindings, source-row provenance, explicit license disposition, and one reasoned Change Set; unresolved references are diagnostics rather than lost data.

An Engineer publishes a semantic edit with expected revision and correlation ID; the transaction creates one Change Set, successor Part and any needed Asset Revisions, a head update, and an Audit Event, while no-op, duplicate, unauthorized, and stale commands behave deterministically.
The desktop shows semantic diff, conflict, and history and restores by creating a new successor revision; a second client converges through PocketBase realtime plus checkpoint reconciliation.

A schema-bearing Catalog Category validates the representative part without changing its stable IPN Family, and an externally observed DigiKey, Mouser, or LCSC category becomes a reviewed mapping rather than an automatic silent reclassification.

The complete source catalog, substitutes, assets, origins, and license declarations import with a zero-loss oracle report and regenerate semantically equivalent staged SQLite and database-library artifacts deterministically.

The checked-in CSV catalog and local libraries remain byte-for-byte unchanged during the isolated canonical pilot; generated projections exist only in test-owned paths, and no Python or PyQt runtime dependency is introduced.

Every Tauri or Leptos state introduced by this epic has an automated native Linux journey, semantic and accessibility assertions, screenshots for materially distinct states, and a recorded agent visual self-review followed by any required iteration.

sections.context: Teams own material distributed across local labs, assembly houses, partner-managed accounts, and stock in transit. Existing planning distinguishes physical carriers and estimated quantities, but it does not yet separate ownership, custody, source, site, restrictions, reservations, or a standing local prototype floor. Without those distinctions, a global available total can over-promise restricted stock, transfers can double-count, aggregate partner balances can gain fictional traceability, and permanent fake reservations make local coverage impossible to reason about. The product plan and Inventory glossary define the required language and low-click progressive-disclosure UX.
sections.approach: Deliver four vertical tracer bullets through the real Rust domain, PocketBase contract boundary, Leptos/Rust-UI surface, and AFK Linux evidence path. Establish a physical Stock Holding and confidence ledger first; then add a partner aggregate position and distributed overview; then prove Material Reservations and project-derived Stock Floors; finally prove restricted-pool transfer and reconciliation. Every slice uses independent Recorded Owner, Custodian, Inventory Site, supplier/source, Stock State, and Use Constraints. Reservations and floors affect demand-specific allocation but never Stock Movements. Common workflows remain compact, while site, carrier, evidence, and history detail appear progressively in a side sheet.

alternatives.name: One global quantity per part
alternatives.rejected_because: It cannot preserve custody, location, confidence, traceability, partner-pool restrictions, or local prototype coverage and would produce unsafe availability answers.

alternatives.name: Treat every external balance as a Stock Container
alternatives.rejected_because: It invents reels, lots, and date codes that the partner did not report and makes reconciliation misleading.

alternatives.name: Represent reservations and local buffers as Stock Movements
alternatives.rejected_because: Neither changes physical quantity or custody; mixing them into the ledger corrupts on-hand arithmetic and obscures their different lifecycles.

alternatives.name: Build schema layers before any user journey
alternatives.rejected_because: Layer-only work delays validation of terminology, policy, integration seams, accessibility, and the low-click UI until the model is expensive to change.

steps.title: Receive and estimate one physical reel end to end
See one part across local and partner-held stock
Protect local prototype coverage while reserving one build
Transfer and reconcile one restricted partner stock pool

risks: Seller/source, Recorded Owner, Custodian, and Inventory Site could collapse into one overloaded vendor or location field.
Expected quantities or stale partner balances could be shown as exact or universally allocatable.
Reservations, Stock Floors, quarantine, or workflow locations could leak back into the physical Stock Movement ledger as dispositions.
Dispatch, destination receipt, and Procurement inbound supply could count the same pieces more than once.
A broad inventory screen could become a scroll-heavy ERP form and violate the product's few-click interaction goal.
Partner adapters could fabricate carrier-level traceability or silently overwrite earlier source evidence.
AFK screenshot comparison could pass while semantics, focus, or demand-specific labels remain wrong.
acceptance: A user can receive, label, observe, and reconcile one physical reel while the immutable ledger preserves quantity confidence and provenance.

One Managed Part can be shown across a local physical holding and a partner aggregate balance with independent Recorded Owner, Custodian, Inventory Site, source, restrictions, freshness, and confidence; no fictional carrier or lot is created.
The overview and part side sheet separate local, partner-held, reserved, protected, quarantined, and in-transit facts and calculate Allocatable Quantity only for a named demand policy.

A user can set a direct local Stock Floor or preview one derived from N builds of an exact Project Revision, then reserve a production build without changing on-hand quantity or silently consuming the floor.
A restricted partner pool cannot satisfy incompatible demand or mix with a prohibited pool; dispatch and receipt move stock through one in-transit position and conserve quantity under retry.

Each child Seed has domain/property tests, real pinned PocketBase adapter coverage where applicable, WebdriverIO browser/native journeys, accessibility assertions, deterministic screenshots and diffs, an agent visual-review note, and a cargo xtask AFK command with retained evidence.
The common Receive, Move, Reserve, and Keep local workflows fit the 1280x800 acceptance viewport with bounded scrolling, keyboard operation, visible exceptions, and no unbounded master form.
Documentation, Inventory glossary, Seed dependency graph, Mulch guidance, and implemented behavior use the same canonical terms and pass their validation commands.

sections.context:
User decisions of 2026-10-10 (seed text, docs/contexts/catalog/CONTEXT.md, mulch mx-5e5fb1 and mx-f75a28): old products must keep the exact parts they were designed with, while new designs use the newest. A part revision is the exact symbol, footprint and 3D model revisions a part uses, and only a CAD change adds one (the same CAD content under a newer CAD item number is not a change; 54d5 already enforces this for bindings). Part details (description, value, datasheet and the other describing fields) and manufacturer parts belong to the IPN and are shared by every revision: changing them is recorded in the history (who, when, why, before and after) but adds no revision. A part that can no longer replace the old one gets a new IPN. Restore goes away; a bad revision is archived: hidden from KiCad and the app, still found by designs that use it, never deleted. The current revision is the newest revision that is not archived. The IPN never carries the revision (KiCad names such as RES-0000-0470_v2 come later in kicad-parts-f397, which this seed blocks).

Today the opposite is built (mx-88ce27). One canonical JSON document per part revision (crates/catalog part.rs PartDetails, schema kicad-parts/part-details/1) holds every describing field, the Symbol and Footprint fields, the manufacturer parts, the CAD bindings (cad_references) and Excluded from BOM. Every edit (catalog_lib.js publishPartRevision) and every CSV change (catalog_csv_imports.pb.js) adds a full revision; POST /api/catalog/restores copies an older document as a new revision; commands carry expectedRevision; the desktop (apps/desktop-ui/src/team.rs, crates/catalog-browser/src/team.rs) shows a revision-only history with Restore; the replica (crates/catalog/src/replica.rs) follows part revisions per Change; the zero-loss report (tooling/catalog-import/src/zero_loss.rs) compares every CSV column with the revision the latest import run left the part at; the write guards (catalog_write_guards.pb.js) let a part's current revision pointer move only forward to the next number. Nothing is deployed, so, following the 54d5 precedent, old local team server data may be refused with a plain start-fresh message.
sections.approach:
SIMPLEST DESIGN, AND WHY

1. Data model: two kinds of immutable, numbered, hashed records per part, both following the rules every Catalog record already follows (never changed, ID derived from content key, SHA-256 of the stored canonical JSON, guard-tested).
- Saved part details: new collection catalog_part_details (part, number from 1 per part, predecessor, change, snapshot, snapshot_sha256, source; ID derive_id('part-details', part + newline + number); unique (part, number)). The snapshot is PartDetails schema kicad-parts/part-details/2: { schema, ipn, fields, manufacturer_parts } with every describing field in source order (Description, Value, Datasheet, Tolerance, Sim_*, Comments, Project link and the rest; never Symbol or Footprint) and the manufacturer parts (main first). Each details change saves the next number. These are never called revisions: the UI says 'Details changed'. The part record gains current_details and current_details_number (the guard allows them to move only to the next number, like today's revision pointer).
- Part revisions: catalog_part_revisions keeps its collection, but its snapshot becomes PartRevision schema kicad-parts/part-revision/1: { schema, ipn, cad_fields, cad_references, excluded_from_bom }. cad_fields holds the Symbol and Footprint fields exactly as written (raw text, so the zero-loss report stays byte-exact; `;` footprint choices included), cad_references the exact CAD item revision each reference binds (unchanged 54d5 rules: keep the bound number while content is the same), and excluded_from_bom moves here because it comes only from CAD flags (how it changes on a new revision stays kicad-parts-ccc0; until then an edit copies it, as today). The cad_item_revisions relation stays.
- History: each saved details record, part revision and (step 3) archive entry points to its Change, so a part's history is those records ordered by Change seq. Before and after are computed: details N against N-1 (compare_details, fields and manufacturer parts) and revision N against its predecessor (new compare_revisions: Symbol, Footprint, bindings, Excluded from BOM). Nothing is stored twice. A Change now holds at least one of: a part revision, a CAD item revision, saved part details, or (step 3) an archive entry; the zero-loss Changes check and the summary counts follow.
Why not a mutable details record plus audit entries with before/after JSON: it would make parts a second kind of mutable record for the guards, the zero-loss report could not find the exact details an import run left a part at without replaying entries, the replica would need the details inside the Change, and nothing would be hash-checked. Immutable saved details reuse every existing mechanism (guards, derived IDs, replay ledger, replica by seq, conflict numbers) for one new collection.

2. How a part revision references CAD only: as above, the revision snapshot has no describing fields and no manufacturer parts. Revision 1 is saved for every new part, even one with no Symbol or Footprint column (g-pcb), so every part has a current revision. A new part revision is saved only when cad_fields, a binding's CAD content (3D models included, through the footprint revision) or excluded_from_bom differ from the current revision. Its predecessor is the newest revision (archived or not), so numbers stay gap-free.

3. Conflict detection for details edits: a command carries the number it started from for each kind of thing it changes, and only what the person changed. POST /api/catalog/edits becomes { correlationId, reason, ipn, details?: { expectedDetails, fields, manufacturerParts }, cad?: { expectedRevision, symbol, footprint } }, with at least one section. The desktop backend (catalog-browser) includes a section only when the person changed something in it compared with the record they started from. The server checks each sent section against its own number: 409 conflict (nothing written, not stored in the ledger) if that number moved, naming which one moved and returning it. So a details edit never conflicts with someone else's CAD revision or an import's CAD change, and the reverse. The details section must list the same field names in the same order as the current saved details (as today's editedDetails), so supplier data and CAD can never enter them. The cad section is bound server-side exactly as cadReferences does today, against the current revision. Both sections in one command make one Change (kind edit) with saved details and a part revision; 422 noop when neither would change. The server trusts nothing: it re-derives every ID, re-hashes every snapshot, builds the snapshots itself from validated values in a fixed order, and computes the request hash from validated values (mx-8f0de0). Field-level automatic merging is left to kicad-parts-5514 (roles and priority are per field); the existing 'Save my changes on top of theirs' screen stays, per section.

4. Migrating existing revisions: refuse, do not convert. New migration 1791800000_shared_part_details.js refuses to start, changing nothing, when any catalog_part_revisions record exists, with the plain message 'this team server's data was saved before part details were kept apart from revisions, and it cannot be upgraded. Nothing was changed. Start again with an empty data folder (see docs/operations/TRY_THE_TEAM_CATALOG.md)'; its undo refuses whenever any catalog_part_details record exists. It creates catalog_part_details, adds the part fields, and sets catalog_changes.kind to [csv-import, edit] (restore removed; step 3 adds archive and unarchive). Converting mixed revisions would mean inventing which edits were details-only and renumbering immutable records, for data nobody has deployed.

5. CSV imports under the new model.
- Columns: Symbol and Footprint are CAD (new ColumnRoute::Cad in crates/catalog csv_import route_column; they feed cad_fields and cad_references). IPN is the identity. MPN and Manufacturer (and substitutes.csv rows) are manufacturer parts. The 7 supplier data columns stay in the source only. MPN2, MPN TBC and unknown MPN columns stay import problems (mx-9a51aa). Every other column, Value, Datasheet and Sim_* included, is a describing field of the part details. Excluded from BOM is no column; it is set in the revision from CAD flags.
- Ownership is per part and per kind (details or CAD), the smallest unit that answers the user's example: a part's details follow the CSV only while its latest saved details came from a CSV import; its CAD follows the CSV only while its current revision came from a CSV import. So if someone edited only the description in the app and the CSV changes the footprint content, the import adds a part revision bound to the new footprint revision and leaves the edited description as it is. If the CSV changes a describing field of a part whose details were edited in the app, nothing is overwritten: an import problem csv-details-differ-from-edited-details keeps the row (kicad-parts-75a5 later lets people accept fields one by one). If the CSV changes the CAD of a part whose current revision came from an app edit, csv-cad-differs-from-edited-revision keeps it. These replace csv-row-conflicts-with-current-revision. Per-field ownership inside the details was considered and rejected for now: knowing what the CSV last said for each field needs a per-run copy of every part's CSV details and makes accepted fields drift back to CSV ownership in surprising ways; the CSV catalog is a source nobody edits (glossary), so changes after an app edit are rare and a field-by-field accept (75a5) is enough.
- The request: parts[] carries expectedRevision and expectedDetails (both 0 for a new part; set only by ImportCommand::expecting, and both part of the derived correlation ID, mx-64c42a), and two documents, details { snapshot, snapshotSha256, source } and revision { snapshot, snapshotSha256, source }. Both sources must be the CSV row the run sends (checked as today). The server checks expectations (409 conflict per part, as today), then decides each kind separately: unchanged (same hash), new record (owned by CSV), or import problem (owned by an app edit). current-revision-without-csv-source becomes current-details-without-csv-source; csv-row-changed-without-part-details-change stays for rows whose only change is supplier data.
- Idempotency: unchanged documents hash the same, existing problems are reused by content ID, and a run with nothing new and the same files is 422 noop, as today. Each run's audit entry records parts as [{ ipn, revision, details }], the numbers it left each part at.
- Zero-loss report: rebuilds the CSV from the latest run as today, then checks describing columns, MPN and Manufacturer against the saved details numbered `details`, and Symbol and Footprint (exact cad_fields text) plus all CAD checks against the revision numbered `revision`. A row may be applied for one kind and kept by an import problem for the other; columns are accounted per kind. New destination part-revision in the column table; the test every_column_of_every_csv_file_has_one_destination and the 21-file pilot must stay lossless.
- read_import_state reads each part's current revision and current details numbers and the CAD the current revision binds (kicad-parts-7828, reading only current records, fits here if it falls out naturally, but is not required).

6. Archive (step 3).
- New collection catalog_archive_entries, append-only: part, part_revision, revision_number, archived (true for archive, false for unarchive), change, current_revision_after; ID derive_id('archive-entry', correlation ID). A revision's state is its newest entry. Change kinds archive and unarchive (migration 1791900000_archived_revisions.js; no data refused, step-2 data stays valid).
- POST /api/catalog/archives { correlationId, reason, ipn, revision, archived }: same people as edits (users.can_edit_catalog and superusers until kicad-parts-5514 gives this to Engineers and the Owner), reason required, one Change and one audit entry. 422 noop if the revision already has that state. Decided (user, 2026-10-10): refuse to archive the last revision that is not archived ('Revision 1 is the only revision that is not archived, so it cannot be archived. Add a corrected revision first.'), so every part always has a current revision; and allow unarchive with a reason, because a wrong click otherwise cannot be fixed.
- Current revision: the server moves catalog_parts.current_revision and current_revision_number to the newest revision that is not archived, in the same transaction; the guard is rewritten to require exactly that (computed in the hook from the transaction's records, mx-3013a8) and still requires a new revision to be newest+1 with the newest as predecessor. The desktop shows the pointer's revision as current and archived revisions only in the history (labelled, with reason) and by IPN plus revision number (previews of an archived revision still work). The replica applies archive entries through current_revision_after, fetching that revision if it does not hold it. Later, kicad-parts-f397 reads the same pointer: current revision in the main library, older non-archived revisions in the older-revisions library, archived ones in a hidden library the part chooser does not show, so designs that use them still find them (decided).
- Imports never bring an archived design back: if the CSV's CAD for a part has the same content as an archived revision of that part, the import adds nothing and records csv-cad-matches-archived-revision (found again by every run, so idempotent).
- Only part revisions are archived in this seed. CAD item revisions keep 'current = newest' (decided): the CSV libraries would add the archived content back on the next import, and KiCad entries per CAD item revision come with f397. To retire a bad footprint revision now, archive the part revisions that use it after adding corrected ones.

7. Removing Restore (step 1, before the remodel so step 2 is smaller): delete POST /api/catalog/restores and its use in catalog_lib.js, RestoreCommand, submit_restore, RESTORE_ROUTE, the TEAM_RESTORE command, TeamRestoreRequest, restore_revision, restored_from and restore_changes in desktop-contract, the Restore form and conflict branch in apps/desktop-ui/src/team.rs and styles, the Tauri command in apps/desktop/src/main.rs, the restore parts of tests (pocketbase_edits, desktop_team, journey 06) and docs (TRY_THE_TEAM_CATALOG.md, module docs, guard comments). Old restore Changes still display as 'Restored' until step 2's migration refuses that data; the restore kind value is removed by that migration.

8. Desktop (keeping the approved look, mx-793b81, reusing styles.css tokens).
- Details tab: 'Part details (shared by every revision)' with Edit details; then 'Revision N (current)' with the symbol and footprint it uses and their CAD item revisions, and a short list of the other revisions (number, older or archived).
- Edit form: details fields and manufacturer parts, plus a separate 'Symbol and footprint' group whose change adds a revision, with the hint 'Change details only to correct them. A part with a different value, package or pinout needs a new IPN.' Save notices: 'Saved. The part details changed; no revision was added.' or 'Saved as revision 3.'
- History tab: one list, newest first, mixing 'Details · Edited by Ada Editor', 'Revision 2 · Imported by an administrator', and (step 3) 'Revision 2 · Archived by Ada Editor', each with when, why and a before/after table. Archive and unarchive forms on a selected revision, with the plain explanation 'KiCad and this app stop offering revision 2, so nobody new picks it. Designs that already use it keep it. Nothing is deleted. The current revision becomes revision 1.'
- Conflict screen: per section ('Someone else changed these details first' / 'Someone else changed the symbol or footprint first'), columns 'You started from', 'Theirs', 'Yours'.
- Screenshots that change, each reviewed with a written critique and approved, never self-accepted (mx-683e0a, mx-312c84): step 1 removes 47-team-restore and 48-team-restored and changes 46-team-history and 49-team-read-only; step 2 changes 42-team-part-details, 43-team-edit, 44-team-live-update, 45-team-conflict, 46-team-history, 49-team-read-only and likely 51-team-preview-stored-revision; step 3 adds 47-team-archive and 48-team-archived and changes 46 and 49 again; step 4 adds the import-problem screens of 75a5.

9. Plain language (ISO 24495; the user approved this wording, applied to CONTEXT.md before step 1): Change: 'One saved update with a reason, such as an import, an edit or an archive. It can change part details and add or archive revisions of several parts and CAD items at once.' Archived: add 'Archiving can be undone, with a reason.' and add 'restore' to its Avoid list. No new noun for saved part details: people see 'Details changed'; code uses catalog_part_details, PartDetails, details number, never 'version' (on the Revision Avoid list). Import problem codes in plain words (csv-details-differ-from-edited-details, csv-cad-differs-from-edited-revision, csv-cad-matches-archived-revision). Messages start with a plain lowercase word (mx-464fd0). Each step updates the docs and mulch records it makes stale (mx-88ce27 superseded by mx-5e5fb1; mx-0075f5, mx-64c42a, mx-c5e787, mx-ee29d9, mx-0a590f, mx-404964 updated).

STEPS IN DETAIL
Step 1, Remove Restore: everything in point 7; journey 06 no longer restores; gate green.
Step 2, Keep part details apart from revisions: points 1 to 5 and 8 (without archive): migration, collections, guards (new collection in every refuse list; details pointer moves only to the next number; revision rules unchanged), PartDetails/2 and PartRevision/1 with tests that the Rust and JS schema tags and kinds stay in step, csv_import split and ColumnRoute::Cad, CsvImport numbered_against for revisions, ImportCommand expectedDetails, the import route, the edit route with sections, read_back and CatalogReadback.part_details, replica holding current revision and current details per part (a Change may hold only saved details), catalog-browser load, history, edit and conflict, desktop-contract, desktop UI, zero-loss report, catalog-import tests rewritten for the new rules (details edits add no revision; a CSV CAD change on a part with edited details adds a revision; edited CAD gives an import problem; re-imports stay idempotent and lossless), journeys 06 and 07. This is the largest step because the snapshot shape is shared by server, importer, replica and desktop; any split would leave a broken or shimmed middle.
Step 3, Archive a revision instead: point 6 end to end, with tamper tests for the new guard and the new collection, a realtime and catch-up test where a Change holds only an archive entry, and screenshots 47 and 48.
Step 4 (kicad-parts-75a5), Accept CSV changes field by field: on a part with a csv-details-differ-from-edited-details problem, list each differing details field and manufacturer parts with both values; accepting saves a normal details edit (no revision) and resolves the problem; on csv-cad-differs-from-edited-revision, accepting adds a part revision; accepting CAD that matches an archived revision is refused. Its seed text ('a new revision with a reason') is updated when adopted.
Step 5 (kicad-parts-ccc0), Excluded from BOM follows the revision's CAD: decided, recalculated from the bound CAD whenever a revision is added, shown read-only on the revision; old designs keep theirs because revisions are pinned.

EXISTING SEEDS
Adopted: kicad-parts-75a5 (step 4) and kicad-parts-ccc0 (step 5) both fit only once details and CAD are separate. Not adopted: kicad-parts-3b8b (edits that upload new CAD item revisions) is a new capability, not part of the model change; it only needs step 2's cad section, so it should be blocked by step 2 and stay its own seed. kicad-parts-7828 and kicad-parts-a3ba (read and catch up only current records) touch code step 2 rewrites; the implementer may close them if their fix falls out naturally, otherwise they stay. kicad-parts-5514 later replaces users.can_edit_catalog for edits and archives.

USER DECISIONS (2026-10-10, all recommendations approved): the last revision that is not archived cannot be archived; archive can be undone (Unarchive, with a reason); only part revisions are archived for now; after an app edit of a part's details, later CSV details changes become an import problem to accept (ownership per part and per kind); Excluded from BOM is recalculated from the CAD of every new revision and shown read-only; the app may edit Value and change Symbol and Footprint, with the new-IPN hint; Sim_* columns are shared part details; in f397 archived revisions go in a hidden KiCad library. The user asked for best judgement on product simplicity and UX without further questions; screenshot changes are approved by the reviewer and orchestrator after inspecting each image against the approved theme.

alternatives.name: Keep part details on a mutable part record and keep their history only as audit entries with before/after JSON
alternatives.rejected_because: Parts would become a second kind of mutable Catalog record for the guards; the zero-loss report could not find the exact details an import run left a part at without replaying entries; the replica would need the details inside each Change; nothing would be hash-checked. Immutable saved details reuse every existing rule and mechanism for one new collection.

alternatives.name: Keep one document per revision but add a revision only when the CAD in it changes, updating details in place
alternatives.rejected_because: Revisions would no longer be immutable, which breaks the guards, the hashes and every reader that checks a snapshot against its SHA-256.

alternatives.name: Convert existing mixed revisions into saved details and CAD revisions
alternatives.rejected_because: Nothing is deployed; converting would mean guessing which edits were details-only and renumbering records that never change. The 54d5 precedent of refusing old data with a plain start-fresh message is simpler and safe.

alternatives.name: Per-field ownership between CSV imports and app edits inside the part details
alternatives.rejected_because: It needs a per-run copy of what the CSV said for every part and makes accepted fields drift back to CSV ownership in surprising ways. Ownership per part and per kind (details or CAD) already answers 'someone edited the description, the CSV changed the footprint', and 75a5 lets people accept other fields one by one.

alternatives.name: Server-side automatic merge of non-overlapping field edits instead of 409 conflicts
alternatives.rejected_because: It belongs with roles and priority (kicad-parts-5514), which decide who wins per field. This seed keeps today's conflict screen, now per section, so a details edit and a CAD change never conflict with each other.

alternatives.name: Store archive state as a flag on the part revision
alternatives.rejected_because: Revisions never change once written. An append-only archive entry keeps that rule, records who, when and why, and makes unarchive a second entry rather than an edit.

alternatives.name: Archive CAD item revisions in this seed too
alternatives.rejected_because: The CSV libraries would add the archived content back as a new CAD item revision on the next import, and per-CAD-item KiCad entries only arrive with f397. Archiving the part revisions that use a bad CAD item revision covers the need now.

alternatives.name: Remodel first and remove Restore in the same step
alternatives.rejected_because: Restore can be removed on today's model in a small, reviewable step, which shrinks the remodel step and its screenshot review.

steps.title: Remove Restore from the server, the desktop, the tests and the docs
Keep part details apart from revisions: details changes add no revision, only CAD changes do
Archive a part revision instead of restoring; the current revision is the newest not archived
Let people accept CSV changes on edited parts, field by field
Recalculate Excluded from BOM from the CAD of each new revision

risks: Step 2 is large: the snapshot shape is shared by the server hooks, the Rust importer, the replica, catalog-browser and the desktop. Mitigation: removing Restore first (step 1) and archive later (step 3); the implementer works in small commits inside the step and the reviewer checks server trust and guards first.

Lossless report: Symbol and Footprint must be kept as exact raw text in the revision (cad_fields), not rebuilt from trimmed references, or the 21-file pilot loses bytes (`;` choices, spaces). A row applied for one kind and kept by an import problem for the other must be accounted per column.

Guard rewrite: the current revision pointer must be allowed to move back on archive and forward on unarchive while still refusing every other move, and a new revision must stay newest+1 with the newest (possibly archived) as predecessor. Needs tamper tests (stop server, edit data.db, restart; mx-404964) and the PocketBase quirks: e.record.original() empty after create-then-save (mx-3013a8), Go map key order in request hashes (mx-8f0de0), capitalised error messages (mx-464fd0), Go string pointers for rules (mx-464fd0).

Content hashing: the 'CSV CAD matches an archived revision' check must use one implementation (the server's contentOf over canonical JSON); the Rust and server content hashes differ and must never be compared (mx-0a590f).

Replica and realtime: a Change may now hold only saved details or only an archive entry; the follower must apply both and catch-up makes up to three requests per Change, which makes kicad-parts-a3ba more urgent at full-catalog size.

Archive moves the current revision back to an older one: KiCad (later) and new picks then get older CAD; the archive form must say which revision becomes current, and the desktop must fetch that older revision's snapshot.
Terms can drift: saved part details must not be called revisions or versions in UI, docs or code names; the reviewer checks every new word against the glossaries' Avoid lists.
Screenshots: most team screenshots change in steps 1 to 3; each change needs an inspected diff and a written critique, never a baseline accepted only because a test changed.
f397 must put archived revisions in a hidden KiCad library so 'Update from Library' still finds them; bd76 keeps archived revisions readable in the Catalog and the app.
acceptance: Every step: the full gate passes on Windows: cargo fmt --all --check; cargo clippy with -D warnings for the native workspace (all targets) and for the desktop UI's wasm32 target; cargo test --workspace --locked; cargo run -q --locked -p csv-catalog-fixture -- check .; catalog-import pilot lossless for each of the 21 CSV files; all hidden desktop journeys pass, and every changed or new screenshot has an inspected diff, a written visual critique and approval by the reviewer and the orchestrator after inspecting the image against the approved theme.

Every step, server trust: every protected route re-derives IDs, re-hashes snapshots, builds stored documents itself from validated values, computes request hashes from validated values in a fixed order, refuses anything the client cannot be trusted with (400), answers conflicts with 409 without writing or storing them, and replays applied and no-op answers byte for byte; tests forge each derived value and show nothing is written.

Every step, guards: every catalog_* collection, old and new, refuses create, update and delete through the record API for everyone including superusers, refuses update and delete from server code except the pointer moves the step defines, and refuses collection changes that would lose data; tamper tests cover each new rule.

Step 1: POST /api/catalog/restores answers 404; no Restore button, form, command, contract type or doc remains (grep finds 'restore' only in history labels for old data and unrelated backup code); journey 06 and desktop_team.rs pass without restoring; screenshots 47 and 48 are removed and 46 and 49 re-approved.

Step 2: an edit that changes only details saves the next saved-details number, adds no part revision, and is shown as 'Details changed' with before and after, who, when and why; an edit of Symbol or Footprint adds exactly one part revision; a details edit does not conflict with a concurrent CAD revision and vice versa, while two details edits from the same starting number give one applied and one 409; old data is refused by the new migration with the plain start-fresh message, changing nothing, and its undo refuses populated data.

Step 2: CSV imports route Symbol and Footprint as CAD and every other describing column to part details; on a part whose details were edited in the app, a CSV footprint content change adds a part revision and keeps the edited description; a CSV details change on that part records csv-details-differ-from-edited-details and changes nothing; a CSV CAD change on a part whose current revision came from an app edit records csv-cad-differs-from-edited-revision; re-running any import is 422 noop or nothing_changed with no new records; the zero-loss report checks details columns against the saved details and Symbol and Footprint against the revision the run left each part at, and stays lossless for all 21 files.

Step 2: the replica and the desktop follow details-only Changes live and through checkpoint catch-up; the results list and part header show the current details and the current revision's symbol and footprint; previews still draw the exact stored CAD item revision.

Step 3: an editor archives a revision with a reason; the part's current revision becomes the newest revision that is not archived, in the server, the replica and the desktop; archived revisions stay readable in the history and by IPN and number, with their previews; unarchiving restores the pointer rule; archiving the last non-archived revision is refused with a plain message; people without edit access get 403; a CSV whose CAD matches an archived revision adds nothing and records csv-cad-matches-archived-revision on every run; screenshots 47-team-archive and 48-team-archived approved.

Step 4 (75a5): a part with a details import problem lists each differing field with both values; accepting chosen fields saves one details edit with a reason, adds no revision and resolves the problem; accepting a CAD difference adds one part revision; unchosen fields stay as they are.

Step 5 (ccc0): Excluded from BOM is recalculated from the bound CAD whenever a revision is added, is shown on the revision in the desktop, is checked by the zero-loss report, and never changes an existing revision.

Docs and records: TRY_THE_TEAM_CATALOG.md, module docs and route comments describe the new model; the approved glossary wording is applied to docs/contexts/catalog/CONTEXT.md; mx-88ce27 is superseded and the mulch records named in the approach are updated by the step that makes them stale.

name: Revisions are CAD changes; shared part details; archive instead of restore
outcomeNote: All five steps merged on 2026-10-11 with high-effort reviews; follow-ups 733c, 7d84 and the BOM wording seed.
